diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, we can assume $V$ admits the following form:
This is analogous to the fact that the optimal vector field in 2-Wasserstein metric is the gradient of some potential function

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the reformulated metric (dL-new) is equivalent to the original Landau metric (dL). The derivation restricts the infimum variable V to the form V = tilde-nabla phi, justified only by analogy with the 2-Wasserstein case. No proof is given that the optimal V in (dL) is of this form. Restricting to V in the range of tilde-nabla shrinks the admissible set and can only increase the infimum, so (dL-new) need not equal (dL). The paper establishes only that (dL-new) follows from (dL) under an unproven restriction on V.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a proof (e.g., via convex duality analogous to the Benamou-Brenier argument) that the infimum in (dL) is attained at some V of the form V = tilde-nabla phi, or explicitly restrict (dL) to V in the range of tilde-nabla and verify the resulting metric supports the gradient-flow interpretation.
issues.overall_effect: The reformulation (dL-new) and the entire derived chain ((djko), (djko_L2), (djko_p), (djko_p2)) may correspond to a different metric than the Landau metric d_L, undermining the gradient-flow and JKO interpretations motivating the method.
issues.title: Unproven equivalence between Landau metric formulations (dL) and (dL-new)
issues.why_classification: The equivalence needs a contained nontrivial convex-duality or direct argument, but the method's variational particle structure and all substantive claims survive if the equivalence is proved or the metric is properly restricted.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $A$ is semi-positive definite, this implies $A(\bv-\bv_*)(\varphi - \varphi_*) = 0$ on the support of $f_* f$.

issues.failure_explanation: From the premise A(bv-bv*)(varphi - varphi_*) = 0 and ker A(bv-bv*) = span{bv-bv_*} one obtains varphi(bv) - varphi(bv_*) parallel to (bv - bv_*) for all pairs in the support. Concluding varphi in span{1, bv} from this pairwise parallelism requires (i) C^1 regularity of varphi to differentiate and (ii) a non-degenerate connected support of f to propagate the condition from pairs to the whole support. Neither hypothesis is stated in the lemma or used in the proof; the step labeled Therefore omits a nontrivial argument and necessary hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, $\varphi \in span\{ \mathbf{1}, \bv\}$ on the support of $f$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add C^1 (or Lipschitz) regularity assumptions on varphi and a connectedness/non-degeneracy assumption on the support of f, and supply the missing argument from pairwise parallelism varphi(bv)-varphi(bv_*) parallel to bv-bv_* to affinity varphi = a*bv + d.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the optimality condition (opt_u1) and the Hamilton-Jacobi equation for lambda rely on this lemma and become unreliable. The paper's key insight that the unknown component of the flow generator is essentially the score function is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Proof gap in Lemma lemma_1: null-space characterization requires unstated hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The repair requires stated regularity and connectivity hypotheses plus a contained nontrivial interpolation argument, but the lemma's conclusion and all downstream uses survive once these are provided.

issues.failure_explanation: The action term d_{i,j} is quadratic in the particle values bu(bv_i) while the log-determinant surrogate h_{i,j} is linear in the gradient nabla bu(bv_i). One can construct a smooth vector field bu with bu(bv_i)=0 at every particle (making all d_{i,j}=0) but nabla bu(bv_i)=-M*I with M arbitrarily large (making h_{i,j} of order -M). The objective then tends to -infinity as M grows, so the infimum is -infinity and no minimizer exists. The same mechanism makes the semi-discrete problem (djko_p) unbounded below.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the infimum in (djko_p2) to a class where the objective is bounded below (e.g., neural networks with a fixed architecture and bounded parameters, or a Sobolev ball on nabla-bu), or add a regularization penalty lambda*||nabla-bu||^2 to the objective. Then verify the minimizer exists and the entropy-dissipation and conservation properties hold for the constrained problem.
issues.overall_effect: The entropy-dissipation claims in prop:added-3(i) and prop:added-4(i) are vacuous since no minimizer exists to satisfy them. The advertised exact entropy dissipation and unconditional stability lack a mathematical foundation. The JKO loss (jko_loss) inherits the same unboundedness.
issues.title: Variational problem (djko_p2) is unbounded below
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a constrained or regularized formulation and a boundedness argument, but the method's variational particle structure and all substantive claims survive once the function class is restricted; no new global proof architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the case when $d = 3$ and $\gamma = -3$, which corresponds to the Coulomb interaction in plasma

issues.failure_explanation: When i=j, A(bv_i - bv_i) = A(0) = C_gamma * |0|^(gamma+2) * Pi(0). For gamma < -2 (including Coulomb gamma = -3) the factor |0|^(gamma+2) is infinite and Pi(0) is undefined (direction-dependent limit), so h_{i,i} is not a finite number. The double sum in (djko_p2) includes diagonal terms, making the objective undefined for soft potentials. The continuous integral in (djko_L2) is finite near bv_* = bv (the singularity is integrable), but the discrete Riemann sum evaluates the integrand at the singular point.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Exclude the diagonal (i=j) from the h_{i,j} sums in (djko_p2), (jko_loss), and the log-determinant update (update_f), a standard convention for discretizing singular kernels in particle methods.
issues.overall_effect: The objective in (djko_p2) and the JKO loss (jko_loss) are not well-defined for the Coulomb case (gamma = -3), which is one of the paper's primary test cases (examples 3 and 4). Prop:added-4's properties rely on the objective being finite.
issues.title: Diagonal terms h_{i,i}^{n+1} are singular for soft potentials (gamma < -2)
issues.why_classification: A short, local fix (exclude i=j from the h sums) makes the objective finite and preserves every claim, guarantee, and advertised scope, including the Coulomb regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds ||grad-l(theta_k) - grad-l_{ij}(theta_{q-1})||^2 by L^2 ||theta_k - theta_{q-1}||^2, but assumption (A.2) only controls ||grad-l_{ij}(theta_2) - grad-l_{ij}(theta_1)|| (smoothness of l_{ij} alone at two points of the same function). The difference grad-l - grad-l_{ij} at the same parameter value is a variance term not controlled by (A.2). A correct bound decomposes the quantity into ||grad-l(theta_k) - grad-l_{ij}(theta_k)||^2 (variance, controlled only by (A.3)) and L^2 ||theta_k - theta_{q-1}||^2 (smoothness), producing an additional (N/B)(M||grad-l||^2 + sigma^2) contribution that the proof omits entirely.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unjustified bound in the proof of sgd_lemma2 with a correct decomposition ||grad-l(theta_k)-grad-l_{ij}(theta_{q-1})||^2 <= 2||grad-l(theta_k)-grad-l_{ij}(theta_k)||^2 + 2L^2||theta_k-theta_{q-1}||^2, use (A.3) and (A.2) to control the two terms, and adjust the descent inequality and thm_opt_conv's constants and step-size conditions accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rate and step-size conditions in thm_opt_conv are unsupported. Including the missing variance term changes the descent inequality and can require substantially more restrictive step-size or problem conditions (e.g., NM/B < 1/2) for the stated rate to hold.
issues.title: Proof gap in Lemma sgd_lemma2: unjustified cross-function gradient bound
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a contained nontrivial proof modification (adding and controlling a variance term via (A.3)), but the overall descent-plus-drift analysis framework and the convergence conclusion survive with modified constants or step-size conditions.
